score.one_liner: Premier grocery-anchored shopping-center REIT, moat 5/10 — but at $73.24 the TTM owner's-earnings yield is only 2.73% (base OE $2.00/share after charging all $435.1M of development & capital-improvement spend), so the weighted IRR is 6.25% with IV@15% of $20.78 and even the super-bull case earns just 9.76%; it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$21. The REIT lens is kinder (FY2026 guided Nareit FFO $4.84–4.88/share, Core Operating Earnings $4.62–4.66/share), but no reading of the filed numbers supports a 15% owner's-earnings return at this price.
score.exit_alert_suppressed_reason: sector model misfit; tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: Grocery-anchored necessity tenancy: >85% of centers grocery-anchored (search results), anchors 98.4% leased — weekly-trip tenancy that is e-commerce-resistant and feeds the shop tenants

Location scarcity in affluent suburbs: ~$150k average household income within 3 miles (search results), premier suburban trade areas where zoning constrains new competing supply; portfolio 96.9% leased / 94.5% commenced with a $41.2M signed-not-occupied rent pipeline (Q2 2026 release)

Demonstrated pricing power: blended cash rent spreads +10.4% in Q2 2026 (+11.8% trailing twelve months), straight-line +19.5%; same-property NOI +5.3% in 2025, guided +3.7-4.1% in 2026; annual escalators in most new leases (search results)

Development platform: $680M in-process at a ~9% blended estimated yield (Q2 2026 release) — building at yields well above acquisition cap rates, funded cheaply by an A-rated balance sheet (pro-rata net debt + preferred / EBITDAre 5.0x; 87.3% of consolidated real estate assets unencumbered, FY2025 10-K)
Returns corroborate a narrow moat: roic_proxy 7.3% / 8.5% / 9.3% / 7.7% in 2022-2025 (fundamentals.json), operating margin ~72% — above a REIT's cost of capital through the cycle so far
moat_against: No network effects or lock-in: leases roll (short shop leases), grocer anchors are powerful counterparties who can relocate or extract concessions at renewal, and anchor consolidation/bankruptcy is a recurring sector hit

Local scarcity is contestable: rival REITs (Kimco, Brixmor, Federal Realty) and private developers can build or redevelop competing centers; the moat is a portfolio of local positions, not a franchise

Rate and cap-rate exposure dominates: bond-like earnings, a guided 100-150bp refinancing drag as maturing debt reprices (search results), and a valuation multiple that compresses when rates rise regardless of operations

Growth is increasingly bought with capital: revenue CAGR is flattered by the all-stock Urstadt Biddle acquisition (closed Aug 18, 2023; +79 properties) and a development ramp from $232.9M (2023) to $435.1M (2025) of annual spend that depresses current owner's earnings; guided per-share growth is ~5% — utility-like
Discretionary tenant tail (restaurants, fitness, services) and geographic concentration — California and Florida together are roughly half of annual base rent (search results)

overrides_applied.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, 2024, 2025 of the last 3 (in fact all years under engine candidate tags). The override value is the LATEST filed year's (FY2025) development-and-capital-improvements spend, because the final base is the TTM pin: ttm.py fills every capex leg with this override (no filed leg exists under its candidate tags), so the pin is only honest at the current spend level — at FY2025's $435,112 thousand the TTM pin is $2.00/share vs a true TTM of $1.98/share computed from filed 10-Q YTD development spend (FY2025 $435,112 − Q1 2025 $101,386 + Q1 2026 $105,071 = $438,797 thousand TTM spend; analysis.md), while at FY2024's $343,368 thousand the pin would read $2.50/share on a capex leg the filings contradict (spend has plateaued at the FY2025 level: Q1 2026 $105,071 thousand vs Q1 2025 $101,386 thousand). Cost of the choice, disclosed: the engine applies the one value to every gap year, so the normalized 3-yr median reads ~$1.82/share — below every filed year — an artifact; the true per-year median at each year's filed spend and filed diluted share count is $2.31/share and the true latest-FY figure is $2.05/share (analysis.md method range). Acquisitions of operating real estate ($104,153 thousand in 2025, $45,405 thousand in 2024, same statements) are excluded, consistent with the engine's convention of excluding PaymentsToAcquireBusinesses from capex for non-REIT filers.

analysis_md:
# REG — Regency Centers Corporation

**STATUS: SCORED — Tier D (2026-10-17, engine v5.4.0).** First pass-1 run. In scope (market cap $13.35B at $73.24, nasdaq_quote_api, engine market_cap_est on the override share count; $13.40B on the dei outstanding count).

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json, or the FY2025 10-K document itself — none are recomputed. Where a "true filed" figure differs from the engine's override-basis history, both are shown and labelled. Q2 2026 and guidance figures are from cited search results (the Q2 2026 earnings release), as noted.

## What it is
A self-administered, self-managed equity REIT (SIC 6798, Florida corporation, S&P 500 member) that owns, operates and develops grocery-anchored neighborhood and community shopping centers in affluent suburban trade areas. As of December 31, 2025 it owned 391 properties and held partial interests in an additional 90 properties through unconsolidated real estate partnerships (FY2025 10-K, Note 1). More than 85% of centers are grocery-anchored (search results); average household income within 3 miles of its centers is ~$150,000 (search results). The portfolio absorbed Urstadt Biddle Properties in an all-stock asset acquisition that closed August 18, 2023 (+79 grocery-anchored properties in the NY/NJ area; UBP holders received 0.347 REG shares per share — search results and 10-K Note 1).

Current trading (Q2 2026 release, via search results): Nareit FFO $1.21 per diluted share in the quarter; same-property NOI +3.8% YoY; same-property leased 96.9% (anchors 98.4%), commenced 94.5%, with ~$41.2M of signed-not-occupied annual base rent in the pipeline; blended cash rent spreads +10.4% in the quarter (+11.8% trailing twelve months). Management raised FY2026 guidance: Nareit FFO $4.84–$4.88/share, Core Operating Earnings $4.62–$4.66/share (midpoint = >5% YoY growth), same-property NOI growth +3.7–4.1%. In-process development and redevelopment: ~$680M of estimated net project costs at a ~9% blended estimated yield. Pro-rata net debt and preferred stock to TTM operating EBITDAre: 5.0x. Quarterly dividend $0.755/share (paid October 2, 2026, per search results).

## Owner's earnings
The preliminary engine run exited 4 with DATA_GAP:capex and DATA_GAP:shares — Regency files neither figure under tags the engine (or ttm.py) reads. Both gaps are cured by filing-sourced overrides from the FY2025 10-K (bounded authority, kind "filing"; full sources and reasons in judgment.json, measured impact in score.json's override_impact):

- **Capex.** Regency tags its capital spending `PaymentsToDevelopRealEstateAssets`, outside the engine's candidate list, so companyfacts shows no capex series at all (the preliminary run's history carried capex as an assumed $0 — the fake base that made the zero-fill comparison print $4.2274/share). The 10-K's own line is "Real estate development and capital improvements": **$435,112 thousand in 2025, $343,368 thousand in 2024, $232,855 thousand in 2023** (consolidated statements of cash flows / MD&A; the 2023 figure is the same line as tagged in companyfacts). The override declares the latest filed year, $435,112,000. Acquisitions of operating real estate ($104,153 thousand in 2025, $45,405 thousand in 2024) are excluded — the engine's convention excludes business acquisitions from capex for non-REIT filers too.
- **Shares.** Companyfacts carries no weighted-average share series for CIK 910606 after FY2020 (the filer tags share counts with dimensions the aggregated facts drop); the engine fell back to point-in-time outstanding counts (184,581,070 / 181,361,454 / 182,902,234 for 2023/24/25). The 10-K EPS note (Note 14) prints diluted weighted average shares of **182,234 thousand in 2025, 183,040 thousand in 2024, 176,371 thousand in 2023** (diluted EPS $2.82 / $2.11 / $2.04). The override declares the FY2025 count, 182,234,000 — in band vs the last filed diluted value (169,460,000 in FY2020), so no ack was needed; the capex override is out-of-band by construction (no filed value exists to band against) and carries an ack_reason.

**True filed owner's earnings (each year at its own filed capex and filed diluted share count):**

| FY | OCF | Capex (dev. & capital improvements) | SBC | Conservative OE | OE/share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 | $719,591,000 | $232,855,000 | $20,075,000 | $466,661,000 | $2.65 |
| 2024 | $790,198,000 | $343,368,000 | $23,504,000 | $423,326,000 | $2.31 |
| 2025 | $827,692,000 | $435,112,000 | $19,459,000 | $373,121,000 | $2.05 |

(OCF and SBC from financials_history.csv; capex from the 10-K line above; share counts from the EPS note above. OE/share is positive in 5 of the last 5 years on any capex basis — dcf_numbers.json.) The trend is the story: operating cash flow compounds (+9.7%, +9.8%, +4.7%) while development and capital-improvement spend nearly doubles in two years, so true OE/share falls every year. The maintenance definition is far kinder — with capex above D&A, its cap at D&A makes FY2025 maintenance OE equal net income, $527,460,000 (financials_history.csv, override basis) — because most of the $435.1M is growth and redevelopment spend, not upkeep. The sweep's conservative definition charges all of it, and this verdict is on that definition.

- **Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q1 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct legs, saved to ttm.json):**
  - OCF: FY $827,692,000 − prior YTD $161,031,000 + current YTD $152,729,000 = **TTM $819,390,000**
  - Capex: **TTM $435,112,000** — every leg override-filled (no filed leg exists under ttm.py's candidate tags), prorated by days, so the TTM capex is exactly the FY2025 filed spend. Cross-check from filed 10-Q YTD development spend (same `PaymentsToDevelopRealEstateAssets` tag, companyfacts): FY2025 $435,112 − Q1 2025 $101,386 + Q1 2026 $105,071 = $438,797 thousand of true TTM spend — the pin's capex leg is within 1% of the filed TTM spend, because spend has plateaued at the FY2025 level (Q1 2026 $105,071 thousand vs Q1 2025 $101,386 thousand).
  - SBC: FY $19,459,000 − prior YTD $4,966,000 + current YTD $5,279,000 = **TTM $19,772,000**
  - Shares (override, used unprorated as the TTM denominator): **182,234,000**
  - **TTM OE total $364,506,000 → base OE/share $2.0002** (base_source: ttm_json). At the true filed TTM spend of $438,797 thousand the same legs give ~$1.98/share — the pin is honest to ~1%.
- The engine's normalized base (3-yr median) reads **$1.8195/share** — an artifact of the mechanics, disclosed here rather than hidden: the single override capex value is applied to every gap year, so the median year (2024) is charged 2025's $435.1M spend instead of its own filed $343.4M. The true per-year median is $2.31/share (table above) and the true latest FY is $2.05/share; the TTM pin ($2.00) sits next to the latest FY and the true TTM (~$1.98), which is why the pin, not the distorted median, is the base. Balance sheet: net debt $4,634,644,000 on a TOTAL:LongTermDebt basis (gross debt $4,739,301,000 less cash $104,657,000, financials_history.csv); net real estate investments $11,660,779,000 (10-K balance sheet); book equity $6,906,890,000. Preferred stock (9,000,000 shares outstanding) sits outside the engine's net debt.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate / narrow
Justification: grocery-anchored necessity centers in affluent, supply-constrained suburbs with demonstrated pricing power (Q2 2026 blended cash rent spreads +10.4%, same-property NOI guided +3.7–4.1% for 2026 after +5.3% in 2025) and a development platform building at ~9% yields — but no network effects or lock-in (leases roll, grocer anchors are powerful counterparties), each center's local position is contestable by rival REITs and developers, returns are rate/cap-rate dominated, and the measured returns corroborate only a narrow moat: roic_proxy 7.3% / 8.5% / 9.3% / 7.7% across 2022–2025 (fundamentals.json) — above a REIT cost of capital, not wide-moat territory, and flattered by a depreciated-cost asset denominator. Operating margin runs ~72% (fundamentals.json); the filer reports no gross-margin split.
- FOR: Grocery-anchored necessity tenancy: >85% of centers grocery-anchored (search results), anchors 98.4% leased — weekly-trip tenancy that is e-commerce-resistant and feeds the shop tenants; location scarcity in affluent suburbs: ~$150k average household income within 3 miles (search results), premier suburban trade areas where zoning constrains new competing supply; portfolio 96.9% leased / 94.5% commenced with a $41.2M signed-not-occupied rent pipeline (Q2 2026 release); demonstrated pricing power: blended cash rent spreads +10.4% in Q2 2026 (+11.8% trailing twelve months), straight-line +19.5%, same-property NOI +5.3% in 2025 and guided +3.7–4.1% in 2026, annual escalators in most new leases (search results); development platform: $680M in-process at a ~9% blended estimated yield — building at yields well above acquisition cap rates, funded cheaply by an A-rated balance sheet (pro-rata net debt + preferred / EBITDAre 5.0x; 87.3% of consolidated real estate assets unencumbered, FY2025 10-K); returns corroborate a narrow moat: roic_proxy 7.3% / 8.5% / 9.3% / 7.7% in 2022–2025 (fundamentals.json), operating margin ~72%.
- AGAINST: No network effects or lock-in: leases roll (short shop leases), grocer anchors are powerful counterparties who can relocate or extract concessions at renewal, and anchor consolidation/bankruptcy is a recurring sector hit; local scarcity is contestable: rival REITs (Kimco, Brixmor, Federal Realty) and private developers can build or redevelop competing centers — the moat is a portfolio of local positions, not a franchise; rate and cap-rate exposure dominates: bond-like earnings, a guided 100–150bp refinancing drag as maturing debt reprices (search results), and a valuation multiple that compresses when rates rise regardless of operations; growth is increasingly bought with capital: revenue CAGR is flattered by the all-stock Urstadt Biddle acquisition (closed Aug 18, 2023; +79 properties) and a development ramp from $232.9M (2023) to $435.1M (2025) of annual spend that depresses current owner's earnings; guided per-share growth is ~5% — utility-like; discretionary tenant tail (restaurants, fitness, services) and geographic concentration — California and Florida together are roughly half of annual base rent (search results).
- CAP at moat 5 = **8.5 years** (dcf_numbers.json): growth holds 2 years, then fades to the 2.5% terminal rate over the CAP.

## DCF — v5.4 final run (2026-10-17)
Final engine pass: moat 5, probabilities 10/25/30/25/10, offsets −14/−7/−2/+3/+10pp, default OE multipliers, `--ttm` pin (base OE/share $2.0002, source ttm_json). Price $73.24.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | −5.43% | 0.75 | Recession: discretionary tenants fail, a grocer anchor goes dark, same-property NOI turns negative while committed development spend stays sticky — OE/share falls outright | $8.83 | 3.85% |
| Bear | 25% | +1.57% | 0.90 | NOI growth slows toward 1–2%, the guided refinancing drag (100–150bp on maturing debt) lands in full, spend holds at ~$435M/yr — OE barely grows | $14.20 | 4.90% |
| Base | 30% | +6.57% | 1.00 | Same-property NOI compounds ~4%, the signed-not-occupied pipeline and development lease-up add on top, and spend plateaus at the FY2025 level — so OCF growth drops almost entirely into OE off the small TTM OE base | $19.42 | 5.94% |
| Bull | 25% | +11.57% | 1.10 | Rent spreads stay double-digit, the $680M pipeline leases up at ~9% yields, spend moderates — OE/share inflects up | $26.25 | 7.28% |
| Super bull | 10% | +18.57% | 1.25 | Spend reverts toward the FY2024 level ($343M) while OCF compounds at the revenue pace — the development-ramp drag disappears | $39.66 | 9.76% |

- **Probability-weighted IV@15% $20.78; weighted IRR 6.25%. Tier by numbers: D. Bear→bull band: D → D** (no TIER_BAND). Hurdle prices: IV@20% $14.51 (Tier A price), IV@25% $11.08 (Tier S price). Upside at 15%: −71.62% — the price is ~3.5x the weighted IV.
- Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 2.73%; terminal-value share of IV@15 19.39%; scenario spread (super-bull / super-bear IV) 4.49x; net debt / normalized OE 12.71x; months since FY end 9.53.
- **Growth-start sanity check (mandatory).** The engine's blended start is 8.57% — revenue-led (rev CAGR 5y 8.86%, rev CAGR 3y 8.27%, latest rev YoY 6.85%) with an OE/share CAGR component of 18.78% that is an artifact: flat override capex makes historical OE track OCF off a small base. Two further distortions are disclosed: the share-count adjustment reads 0.00 because the shares override flattens the share series (the preliminary run, on filed counts, applied −2.21pp; on the EPS note's filed WASO the count grew +1.65%/yr over 2023–25 after the UBP issuance, so an adjusted blend would sit roughly 1–2pp lower), and the revenue CAGRs themselves are flattered by the August 2023 UBP acquisition. Against actual prints — TTM revenue +7.76% YoY and TTM OCF +4.6% YoY (fundamentals.json), FY2025 revenue +6.85%, same-property NOI guided +3.7–4.1% and Core Operating Earnings guided to >5% growth (search results) — the raw blend is too hot for a per-share OE start. The offsets were therefore shifted −2pp from the default spacing, putting the base start at **6.57%**: still above the NOI and Core-EPS guides, justified only by the fixed-capex leverage in the base story (at a plateaued ~$435M spend, OCF growth falls almost entirely into the $364.5M TTM OE base). If spend instead resumes growing with OCF, OE growth collapses toward the bear start (+1.57%) — that asymmetry is why bear and super-bear carry 35% combined probability. The bull (+11.57%) and super-bull (+18.57%) starts sit above every recent print by construction — they are tails that require the spend drag to reverse — and even the super-bull earns only a 9.76% IRR at $73.24: **the price, not the growth debate, decides this verdict.**

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **DATA_GAP:capex / DATA_GAP:shares** (preliminary run): cured by the two filing-sourced overrides above (FY2025 10-K cash flow statement / MD&A for capex; Note 14 EPS table for shares). data_gap_uncovered is empty in the final run; both overrides are registered with measured impact (override_impact: zero-fill base $4.2274/share and zero-fill weighted IRR 9.81% vs final base $2.0002/share and 6.25% — the zero-fill world is the one where development spend is free, which is exactly the fake this gate exists to stop).
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago): resolved by construction — ttm.py was run (ttm.json saved) and the final pass used the `--ttm` pin; the TTM legs are quoted in full above, and the capex leg was cross-checked against filed 10-Q YTD spend (~$1.98/share true TTM vs the $2.0002 pin). Note companyfacts stops at Q1 2026 — the Q2 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-08-03) is not yet in companyfacts (fundamentals.json warning) — so the freshest filing-direct TTM is through Q1 2026; the Q2 2026 release figures (FFO $1.21/share, same-property NOI +3.8%, guidance raised) show the same trend continuing, nothing that would lift a 2.73% OE yield toward a 15% hurdle.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023): structural REIT bridge, not a one-off. FY2023 net income $364,557,000 + D&A $352,282,000 = $716,839,000 vs OCF $719,591,000 — within 0.4% (financials_history.csv); the residual is the $20,075,000 SBC add-back in OCF and gains on real-estate sales removed from it. 2023 was also the UBP closing year (August 18, 2023), but that transaction was non-cash stock ($818,530 thousand of common stock and $225,000 thousand of preferred stock exchanged for UBP shares, 10-K supplemental disclosures) and distorts investing/financing shape, not operating cash flow. No tax-deposit or impairment distortion was found (real-estate impairment in 2023: $0, companyfacts). The base is OCF-built, so the divergence does not contaminate it; GAAP net income simply understates a REIT's cash generation.
- **SHARES_FALLBACK** (no diluted count filed for 2016, 2021, 2022): in the final run those history years are filled by the shares override (financials_history.csv records OVERRIDE), so their per-share history uses 182,234,000 shares vs the ~171M shares actually outstanding then — OE/share for 2016/2021/2022 is understated by roughly 6%. History only: the base (TTM pin) and the gated years use the filed FY2025 count, and the growth blend's OE-CAGR window (2023–2025) uses filed counts throughout.
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Real Estate): accepted in full — the OE/capex DCF fits REITs poorly, because most of Regency's $435.1M of annual spend is development and redevelopment at ~9% yields (growth capex), not maintenance, and the sweep's conservative definition charges all of it; the maintenance definition above shows the gap. Confidence is graded **low** and the tier reads as "fails the standardized conservative OE screen at this price," not "the centers lose cash." On the REIT lens the company guides FY2026 Nareit FFO to $4.84–$4.88/share and Core Operating Earnings to $4.62–$4.66/share (search results) against a $73.24 price — a buyer is paying a full multiple of guided FFO for ~5% guided per-share growth, so the sector lens softens the D but does not overturn it. The dividend tells the same story: declared DPS TTM $2.92/share with 12 consecutive growth years and no cut since 2010 (fundamentals.json), but dividends paid TTM of $659,795,000 are ~1.8x TTM conservative OE of $364,506,000 — covered on an FFO basis, not by owner's earnings after all capital spend. Share issuance TTM was $98,215,000 with no filed buybacks (fundamentals.json) — mild net issuance on top of the dividend.
- **OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex / OVERRIDE_APPLIED:shares**: the two overrides above; both kind "filing," sourced to the FY2025 10-K document, both unblock the tier (there is no tier without them — but the tier they unblock is D, and the zero-fill alternative they replace printed a flattering 9.81% weighted IRR, so neither override is doing the verdict any favors). The capex override's out-of-band flag is by construction (no filed value under engine tags exists to band against) and carries an ack_reason in judgment.json.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 4.49x super-bear IV): mechanical on a 2.73% OE-yield base with an 8.5-year fade — small base, long duration. Confidence is already low (sector mismatch) and is not raised. The spread does not change the verdict: the bear→bull band is D → D and every scenario, super-bull included, is Tier D.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (net debt 12.71x normalized OE): the multiple is computed against the artifact-depressed normalized OE ($1.8195/share); on the filing's own terms this is ordinary investment-grade REIT leverage — net debt $4,634,644,000 (TOTAL:LongTermDebt basis) against net real estate investments of $11,660,779,000 (10-K), pro-rata net debt + preferred / EBITDAre of 5.0x at Q2 2026 (release), 87.3% of consolidated real estate assets unencumbered (10-K). The warning still applies in OE terms: debt service is senior to a thin 2.73% OE yield, preferred dividends sit outside the engine's net debt, and the guided 100–150bp refinancing drag on maturing debt (search results) pressures OE growth directly — it is priced into the bear cases.

## My thoughts / overlay
- This is a genuinely good REIT priced like one. The operating story is the strongest in the open-air retail sector: necessity tenancy, double-digit cash rent spreads, a signed-not-occupied pipeline, and a development machine that builds at ~9% into a market that buys stabilized centers at much lower yields. None of that is in dispute — it is also all in the price, several times over on an owner's-earnings basis.
- The honest tension is the capex line. Charging all $435.1M of development and capital improvements against OE treats a growth program as upkeep; the maintenance definition (OE = net income, $527,460,000 in FY2025) treats none of it as upkeep. The truth for a shopping-center owner sits between — tenant improvements, leasing commissions and building capex recur even in a no-growth world (the 10-K's own capital-expenditures table breaks the $435.1M into land, building and tenant improvements, redevelopment and development) — but no split in the computed outputs separates them, so no middle base was invented. Method range, all on filed figures: TTM at true filed spend ~$1.98/share → IRR ~6%; TTM pin $2.0002 → 6.25%; true per-year median $2.31/share → still Tier D (the zero-fill companyfacts read, the only flattering one, printed 9.81% and is Tier D itself). **Every defensible base gives Tier D.** No tier override.
- What would change the tier: the development ramp actually ending — filings in which development and capital-improvement spend falls back toward the FY2023 level (~$233M) while OCF holds, which would roughly double OE/share from the TTM base — or the price falling toward the low $20s. At $73.24 the buyer is underwriting the FFO multiple and the ~5% guided Core growth, and needs cap rates to cooperate; the OE screen has nothing to add beyond "not at this price."
- Data note (non-blocking): companyfacts had not yet absorbed the Q2 2026 10-Q at run time, so fundamentals/ttm stop at Q1 2026 (see the flags above); the enrichment files carry the same warning.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (tier by numbers D, band D → D — weighted IRR 6.25% at $73.24; no scenario, including super-bull at 9.76%, reaches the 10% Tier C line, let alone the 15% hurdle)
- Confidence: **Low** (sector-model mismatch: a REIT in a development ramp is exactly where the standardized OE screen is roughest — though the tier is D on every defensible base, including the REIT's own guided FFO lens read generously)
- One-liner: Premier grocery-anchored shopping-center REIT, moat 5/10 — but at $73.24 the TTM owner's-earnings yield is only 2.73% (base OE $2.00/share after charging all $435.1M of development & capital-improvement spend), so the weighted IRR is 6.25% with IV@15% of $20.78 and even the super-bull case earns just 9.76%; it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$21. The REIT lens is kinder (FY2026 guided Nareit FFO $4.84–4.88/share, Core Operating Earnings $4.62–4.66/share), but no reading of the filed numbers supports a 15% owner's-earnings return at this price.
